sections.heading: Invoices and receipts
sections.text: Monthly invoices are issued on the first UTC day of each billing period. Workspace owners can download signed receipts from Billing History. Invoices are payable in USD by card or bank transfer.

sections.heading: Failed payments
sections.text: A failed renewal payment starts a seven-day grace period. The billing service retries on days two and five. At the end of the grace period, editors lose write access until the payment clears.

sections.heading: Annual subscription cancellations
sections.text: An annual subscription may be refunded within fourteen calendar days of the initial purchase. Renewals are excluded from this refund window. Finance normally processes an approved refund within five business days.

sections.heading: Service credits
sections.text: Approved service credits appear on the next invoice as a line item. Credits cannot be exchanged for cash and do not change the workspace renewal date.

sections.heading: Portable workspace archive
sections.text: Workspace owners can request a data export from Data Controls. The archive contains task history and attachments in a ZIP file. A signed download link expires twenty-four hours after it is issued.

sections.heading: Export delivery
sections.text: Export requests are queued and normally complete within four hours. The workspace owner receives a notification when the archive is ready. Exports that fail are retried automatically once.

sections.heading: Snapshot retention
sections.text: Production databases are snapshotted every six hours. Daily snapshots are retained for thirty days in the same residency region. Workspace exports are independent of operational backups.

sections.heading: Disaster recovery objectives
sections.text: The recovery point objective is six hours and the recovery time objective is eight hours. For a restore, the incident commander selects the most recent verified snapshot.

sections.heading: Account closure
sections.text: Closing a workspace disables access immediately. The deletion queue purges active customer data after thirty days unless a preservation hold applies. A closure request can be withdrawn by its owner during that interval.

sections.heading: Long-term storage
sections.text: Aggregated usage counters that contain no workspace identifiers may persist for twelve months. Encrypted recovery copies expire according to the backup retention policy.

sections.heading: Major outages
sections.text: A severity-one incident means a broad loss of core customer functionality. The incident commander opens a coordination channel and posts status updates every thirty minutes while the outage is active.

sections.heading: Retrospectives
sections.text: The incident owner publishes a blameless retrospective within five business days of resolution. Include a timeline, contributing factors, and one accountable owner per mitigation.

sections.heading: Priority support
sections.text: Professional plan support is staffed on weekdays from 09:00 to 18:00 UTC. Enterprise customers can contact support at any hour for critical service interruptions. Standard requests are prioritized by impact.

sections.heading: First response
sections.text: An Enterprise ticket marked critical has a one-hour initial response target. The response target measures the first human acknowledgement and is independent of incident status update cadence.

sections.heading: Uptime target
sections.text: Enterprise subscriptions have a 99.9 percent monthly uptime target. Scheduled maintenance announced at least forty-eight hours in advance is excluded from the uptime calculation.

sections.heading: Credit claims
sections.text: Customers must submit a service credit request within thirty calendar days of the affected month. The service desk verifies eligible downtime and sends approved claims to Finance.

sections.heading: Retries
sections.text: The delivery service retries non-success responses with exponential backoff for up to twenty-four hours. After that window, the event is parked in the dead-letter queue and an alert is sent to the owner.

sections.heading: Duplicate deliveries
sections.text: Webhook consumers should deduplicate requests using the event ID. A single event may be delivered more than once after a receiver responds too slowly.

sections.heading: Rate limits
sections.text: The public API allows six hundred requests per minute per workspace. Requests above the allowance receive HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header. Bulk operations are subject to the same workspace limit.

sections.heading: Request keys
sections.text: Include an idempotency key when creating an invoice from the API. The service remembers accepted key and payload pairs for twelve hours, then permits the key to be used again.

sections.heading: Federated access
sections.text: Enterprise workspace administrators can enable SAML single sign-on. Once enforcement is active, new members authenticate through the company identity provider. The primary owner keeps an emergency local login.

sections.heading: Session policy
sections.text: An interactive session expires after eight hours without activity. Administrators can revoke current sessions from the membership console. Session expiration is distinct from email invitation expiration.

sections.heading: Invitations and roles
sections.text: An emailed workspace invitation expires after forty-eight hours. Owners can resend invitations. Administrators manage members, editors modify tasks, and viewers have read-only project access.

sections.heading: Ownership handover
sections.text: Ownership can be transferred only to an existing administrator. The current owner confirms the handover through a one-time verification code and becomes an administrator.

sections.heading: Supported regions
sections.text: New Enterprise workspaces are provisioned in Frankfurt or Virginia. Project data and attachments remain in the assigned region. Data residency is selected during setup.

sections.heading: Workspace migrations
sections.text: A workspace cannot change region in place. The owner can arrange a migration to a new workspace through Enterprise support. The team agrees on a downtime window before transfer.

sections.heading: Trial duration
sections.text: A trial workspace lasts twenty-one days. No credit card is required to start the trial. The workspace becomes read-only when the trial ends.

sections.heading: Trial extensions
sections.text: Sales can extend an active trial once for up to seven days. Extensions must be requested before the original expiry date.

sections.heading: Summary emails
sections.text: The activity digest is sent every Monday at 08:00 in the recipient's configured time zone. Users can opt out of the digest in Notification Preferences.

sections.heading: Delivery channels
sections.text: Workspace announcements can be delivered in-app or by email. An administrator can mute announcements for low-priority projects. Critical system notifications remain enabled.

sections.heading: Index freshness
sections.text: New task content becomes searchable within five minutes under normal conditions. Index updates are asynchronous. Direct task links stay available while the search index catches up.

sections.heading: Archived tasks
sections.text: Archived tasks are omitted from default search. Users can include archived tasks using the Archive filter. Deleted task records are removed from search automatically.

sections.heading: Maintenance notice
sections.text: Maintenance notifications are sent by email and posted on the status page at least forty-eight hours in advance. The message gives the affected region and estimated maintenance period.

sections.heading: Release windows
sections.text: Routine releases start on Tuesday or Thursday between 01:00 and 03:00 UTC. A release manager may postpone a deployment during an active incident.

sections.heading: Guest restrictions
sections.text: Guests can view and comment on projects explicitly shared with them. Guests cannot manage billing or invite members. A guest can be promoted to a workspace viewer by an administrator.

sections.heading: Public links
sections.text: A public project link exposes the selected project in read-only mode. Workspace administrators can disable existing public links from the sharing console.
